Theme

Nature & food

nature noun

the natural world, as against what people make

also the natural world, the environment, natural environment, in nature, love of nature, Mother Nature

classical

Varr. RR 3.1.4: dīvīna nātūra dedit agrōs, ars hūmāna aedificāvit urbēs
Traupman 156, 349

nātūra, nātūrae f.

noun, first declension

nature: the world as it is made, not built by people

Nature as the maker and order of things, set against human skill (ars): sīc nātūra sōlitārium nihil amat (Cic. Amic. 88). For “I love nature” Morgan–Owens suggests juvat rūsticārī or libenter in silvīs ac campīs versor (see countryside).

Other words

  • rērum nātūra, rērum nātūrae f. — nature as a whole, the physical world

    noun, first declension, with a genitive · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.154: in perspiciendā cognōscendāque rērum nātūrā; Caes. BG 6.14.6: dē rērum nātūrā; Traupman 349: nature (physical world)

    Lucretius’s and Cicero’s phrase for the whole of nature, the subject of natural science. Morgan–Owens takes it, with a query, from Egger for the natural world as against what people make.

  • ambitus nātūrālis — the natural environment

    phrase · also used · modern · M-O s.v. ecology: (natural) environment (Egger, queried)

    Egger’s coinage for “the environment”, which Morgan–Owens marks as doubtful. Classically ambitus is a circuit, the space left round a house, and above all illegal canvassing for votes (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • dīvīna nātūra dedit agrōs, ars hūmāna aedificāvit urbēs

    divine nature gave us the fields, human skill built the citiesVarr. RR 3.1.4

  • nec sōlem proprium nātūra nec āera fēcit nec tenuēs undās: ad pūblica mūnera vēnī

    nature made neither the sun nor the air nor clear water anyone’s own: I have come to a gift that belongs to allOv. Met. 6.350–351

See also countryside, world, environment, nature, animal, tree.

SourcesLewis & Short: natura · Lewis & Short: res · Lewis & Short: ambitus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: ecology: (natural) environment; ecology: nature.
